The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-844/ CR / 36 / 2021-22 dated 15.03.2024 pertaining to Survey No.116 measuring 2910 Square Meters of Neraluru village, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Urban District.
A.P. No.23/2024 .2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 measuring 2910 Square Meters in Survey No.116 of Neraluru village, Anekal Taluk has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020.

The valuation of trees and structure were carried out by the Horticulture Department & Chartered Engineers and the respondent No.3 has passed the award and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.1,71,30,712/- in respect of 2910 Square Meters, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 27.09.2021 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5 crores per acre.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator held an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 /
CR / 36 / 2021-22 dated 15.03.2024.

:GROUNDS:

Point:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Sri.
S. Madhusudan is an owner of the property bearing Survey No.116 measuring to an extent of 2910 Square Meters of Neraluru village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-844 under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020, is an admitted fact.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.1,71,30,712/- was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation in respect of 2910 Square Meters.

.9. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No.1 Sri. S. Madhusudan filed an application on 27.09.2021 before the respondent No.2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.5 crores per acre.
On basis of the said application, the respondent No. 2 hold an inquiry and passed order in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / A.P. No.23/2024 CR / 36 / 2021-22 dated 15.03.2024.

The respondent No.2 in its order enhanced the compensation from Rs. 1,853.22 per Sq. Meters to Rs.2,780.22 per Square Meters and hence the respondent No.2 redetermined the market value at 150% of the amount awarded by the respondent No.3.
.10.

In the case on hand, the LAO/ respondent No.3 passed the award under New Act i.e., Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of market value of the land by the Collector, Section 27 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of amount of compensation,
Section 28 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 A.P. No.23/2024 speaks about parameter considered by the Collector in determination of the award and Section 29 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of value of the things attached to the land or building.
Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act speaks about award of solatium.

In the context of this case, it is just and relevant to note Sections 26 and 28 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, that reads as under:
"26. Determination of market value of land by Collector- (1) The Collector shall adopt the following criteria in assessing and determining the market value of the land,
namely:--
(a) the minimum land value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated; or (b) the average sale price for similar type of land situated in the nearest village or nearest vicinity area; or (c) consented amount of compensation as agreed upon under sub-section (2) of section 2 in case of acquisition of lands A.P. No.23/2024 for private companies or for public private partnership projects, whichever is higher:
Provided that the date for determination of market value shall be the date on which the notification has been issued under section 11".
"28. Parameters to be considered by Collector in determination of award -

sentences.text: The first schedule to the Act is in accordance with Section 30(2) of the New Act which shows that the Collector shall issue individual awards detailing the particulars of compensation payable and the details of payment of the compensation as specified in the first schedule.

In the aforesaid facts whenever there is an application for enhancement of compensation before the Arbitrator is filed then it is the duty of the Arbitrator to see that whether the LAO followed Sections 26 to 30 of the New Act along with first schedule to the Act.
If at all the award has been passed in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law/new Act, certainly the Arbitrator cannot intervene with the award passed by A.P. No.23/2024 the LAO.

Therefore, in the case on hand, it is for the petitioner to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law and the respondent No.1 has to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is not in consonance with the aforesaid provision of law.
As such, he has filed the petition before the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2 by considering all those facts enhanced the compensation.

.12. The definite grievance of the petitioner in this case is that the arbitrator applied 1.5 multiplier though the said multiplication is applicable to the land to the extent of only 5 guntas and the said multiplication is not applicable to this case as the extent of property is more than 5 guntas.

The petitioner also claimed that the Arbitrator has added 50% to the market value holding that acquired land is abutting to National Highway but the claim of the petitioner is that it is the newly formed highway on the acquired land and the land of the petitioner is acquired for formation of A.P.
No.23/2024 highway, as such, there is no possibility of abutting highway to the property of respondent No. 1.
Hence question of adding 50% of the market value of the property of the petitioner does not arise.
The contention raised by the petitioner is that the market value was determined, hence special instructions for enhancement of compensation is not applicable to the property of the petitioner.

In view of these contentions the petitioner has to prove that the property of the respondent No.1 has been acquired for formation of new road and value of the property of the National Highways Authority Of India vs Madhusudan S on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147483051/

Per contra, the respondent No. 1 has to prove that his property was abutting to the national highway prior to the acquisition of property and he is entitled for enhancement as per the special instructions as the competent authority have not declared the market value of the acquired property.
.13.
As per the Gazette notification dated 05.12.2018, 1.5 multiplication is applicable only to the property that will not exceed more than 5 guntas.
The A.P. No.23/2024 property involved in this case is almost 29 guntas, hence the said multiplication certainly not applicable to the present case on hand.

.14. The petitioner claims that the land involved in this case is acquired for new project and there was no existing highway so that the Arbitrator can add additional 50% of compensation but there is no material such as sketch that shows the identification of property in which the project stated in the petition had been carried out.
Hence the said contention of the petitioner cannot be accepted in this case.
.15. The petitioner during the course of arguments has produced the gazette notification dated 05.12.2018 regarding the fixing of market value / guidance value.
As per the said document, the property involved in this case i.e., property in Sy.No. 116 of Neraluru village comes under the potential Zone for which value is fixed at Rs. 75 lakhs per acre.
As per condition No. 4, in the guidance value the 50% or respective enhancement of 35, 30 or 25 percent can be A.P. No.23/2024 added if the guidance value is not fixed.
When the guidance value is fixed, question of adding aforesaid percentages certainly does not arise.
.16. I have closely perused the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2.

The Arbitrator till the 1st paragraph at page No.5 of her judgment not stated any reason for her award but only stated about the respective contentions of the parties as well as acquisition of property by issuing notifications and it is simply stated that there is a discrimination in awarding the compensation and it is stated that first some claimants the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.1,853/- per Square Meter but in this case awarded only Rs. 2,780/- per Square Meter but the entire judgment nowhere discloses for which property and in which case the LAO had awarded compensation at Rs.2,780/-
per Square Meter.
Apart from that what is the nature of property in which the LAO granted compensation of Rs. 2,780/- per Square Meter.
Even as per the guidance value, there are different rates are A.P. No.23/2024 fixed for different properties.

Under such circumstances without specifying the cases in which the aforesaid compensation is granted and if the lands in such cases are not equivalent to the property involved in this case certainly the said compensation cannot be awarded.
Therefore, the said reason of LAO for enhancement of compensation of Rs. 927/- per Square Meter as a difference of some other cases cannot be accepted in this case.

.17. The claim of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 passed the award in accordance with Sections 26 to 30 as well as first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

.18. It is also not the grievance of the respondent No.1 in the application for enhancement of compensation that the respondent No.3 / LAO has not granted the compensation as contemplated under the aforesaid provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

.19. It is also not the case of the petitioner before the LAO or Arbitrator that the respondent No.3 /

The award /
judgment A.P. No.23/2024 passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.

sentences.text: The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.

When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.

sentences.text: The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 A.P. No.23/2024 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO has passed individual award by considering all the relevant facts.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
In view of all these facts, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator cannot be accepted and that should be intervened by the Court.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.
